beats.narration_text: Hallo. This is Liam, in for Bear. A colleague of mine asked an AI to write her whole twenty-page grant proposal in one prompt. What came back looked finished — and fell apart the moment she read it. Here’s the three-part method that holds a long document together.

show.event: backspaces the trigger and types 'Help me outline our grant proposal first.' on the spoken correction

props.replacementWords: Help me outline our grant proposal first

beats.motion_claim: The writer types the naive write-it-all-at-once question and corrects it into the film's method: outline first.

qc.sparse_reason: Hesitant-writer bookend: the correction is the motion.

beats.narration_text: Three terms. An outline: the skeleton of the document, every part in order. A section: one chapter’s worth. And a stitch: reading it as one piece and fixing the seams. That’s all you need for this film.

beats.narration_text: Start with the goal. A twenty-page grant proposal: the need, the plan, the budget, the team — one document that reads like one person wrote it. That is the long game.

beats.narration_text: So she asked for the whole thing in one prompt. Out came twenty pages in thirty seconds — and the middle repeated the beginning, page twelve contradicted page three, and the tone wandered off. Written all at once, a long document drifts.

shot.visual_intent: The neat stack bursts into five scattered pages; the label 'all at once' lands; terracotta dots flag the repeated pair and the contradicted page.

beats.narration_text: Here’s why. Nobody can keep twenty pages straight in one pass — not even an AI. By page fourteen it has forgotten page three. Facts drift, sections repeat, the tone wobbles. A long document is really five short ones stapled together. So write it that way.

shot.visual_intent: Three pages in a row, numbered 3, 9, 14; the label 'it drifts'; repeat dots on page 9, a changed-fact dot on page 14; a staple draws across them.
shot.motion_claim: Three pages in a row, numbered 3, 9, 14; the label 'it drifts'; repeat dots on page 9, a changed-fact dot on page 14; a staple draws across them.

beats.narration_text: Move one: the outline. Before any prose, ask the AI for a section-by-section skeleton — every part, in order. Then you do the most important job in this film: read it, fix it, approve it. The outline is the contract.

shot.visual_intent: The drift pages fade; the outline card lands; its four section rows draw in; a terracotta check stamps your approval; the label 'move one: outline'.
shot.motion_claim: The drift pages fade; the outline card lands; its four section rows draw in; a terracotta check stamps your approval; the label 'move one: outline'.

beats.narration_text: Move two: one section at a time. The AI writes section one — only section one — with the outline beside it. Small enough to check in one sitting, because you read it before the next one starts.

shot.visual_intent: The outline card slides left; the section-one page drops in; an arrow draws card to page; the label 'move two: sections'; a check lands on the page.
shot.motion_claim: The outline card slides left; the section-one page drops in; an arrow draws card to page; the label 'move two: sections'; a check lands on the page.

beats.narration_text: Move three is the handoff. Section two gets the outline plus section one, so the facts stay consistent. Each section carries what the last one said. That is what keeps page fourteen agreeing with page three.

shot.visual_intent: Section two drops below section one; one arrow draws outline to section two, another section one to section two; a check and the label 'move three: the handoff'.
shot.motion_claim: Section two drops below section one; one arrow draws outline to section two, another section one to section two; a check and the label 'move three: the handoff'.

beats.narration_text: Then the stitching. Read the whole thing end to end — out loud if you can — and fix only the seams: the transitions, a repeated sentence, a tone that shifts. You are not rewriting. You are making five sections read like one document.

shot.visual_intent: Three numbered sections line up; a terracotta scan line sweeps down them; the repeated line lifts out and fades; the label 'the stitching'.

beats.narration_text: Same proposal, same AI. On the left: the one-prompt version — twenty pages that fall apart. On the right: outline first, sections one at a time, stitched at the end. A document that holds together.

beats.narration_text: Make it a habit. Outline first. One section per prompt. Stitch at the end. Anything longer than you can check in one sitting is a long game — play it in three moves.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I’m writing a twenty-page grant proposal for a community food bank. Don’t write any of it yet. First, draft a detailed section-by-section outline, then wait for my approval. Then check two things yourself. Does the AI give you an outline instead of prose? And is every part of the proposal on it — nothing missing, nothing extra?
